You are a clinical information extraction system. Read ONE outpatient consultation transcript (lines like "[SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): text") and return ONE JSON object with the clinical information it contains, in the trained clinical-extraction format. Return only the JSON.

Rules
- Use only what is said. Never invent or infer. Leave out every field and section that has no information.
- Record who said it (doctor, patient, nurse, caregiver, family_member, clinical_staff, unknown), in lower case.
- A denied finding goes in negative_findings, never in symptoms. A doctor's question is not a fact: use the answer.
- A medicine the patient takes is not an allergy. A stopped medicine is not current. Dose, frequency, route and indication belong only to the medicine they were said for.
- Doctor impressions are provisional or differential, and only if the doctor stated one. Do not add a diagnosis the doctor declined to give.
- Use the right status for plan items (planned, completed, recommended, conditional). Do not add a follow-up that was not arranged.
- If speakers disagree or a detail is unclear (dose, date, allergy, name), keep both statements and describe the real doubt in clinical_uncertainties.
- Cite one or two segment ids per item in evidence_ids. clinical_evidence is []. All confidence fields are null.

Transcript (encounter 20004)
[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Hi doctor, am I too early?
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): No problem at all, come in. What's troubling you?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): I've been misplacing things.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's run through your medicines.
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Ah I'm on something called losa... losartan 50 milligrams maybe once a day for my blood pressure.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): is the packet here, or the prescription?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): not with me. I'll bring it next time. I take rosuvastatin, 10 milligrams, at night
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): did it come on recently?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): for about a year I'd say i've also been repeating the same question
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): so, what about a low mood, have you noticed that?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): yes about the same three weeks. As for low mood mild I'd say
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): nothing like bladder problems?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No bladder problems.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): alright, a a few quick ones: headache, hallucinations, falls or head injury?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No, none of those at all.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): okay, is your digestion otherwise okay?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): bowels are regular, nothing odd
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any surgery in the the past?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): yes, I had keyhole surgery on my gallbladder, two years back i thought it would sort itself out, but it hasn't
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you react to any medicines or foods? Any allergies?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): No allergies at all.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): any health conditions I should have on record?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes high blood pressure.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): I've got high cholesterol.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about your routine, work, habits, that sort of thing.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): I live with my elderly mother. I drink a lot of tea and snack through the day. I do a yoga class on Thursdays
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): has anyone in your family had anything serious?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): my uncle has high cholesterol
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): shall I check your blood pressure and pulse?
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): okay this won't take long..
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay: height 157 centimetres, heart rate 74, respiratory rate 16, weight 88 kilos, BMI works out to 35.7, pressure 117 over 70, temp 36.5 degrees.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, let's have a proper look at you.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm just checking this side
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): The memory test score is a little low today and the rest of the neurological check is normal.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): All finished, thank you.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's get a memory test, for memory loss. Let's book blood tests to look into memory loss. Keep a daily routine and write things down, a notebook by the door works well. I think the older adults' assessment service should see you too. And please bring the latest prescription or the medicine boxes to the next visit, so we can settle the dose. A brain scan is something we might do if this doesn't improve next month.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep an eye out, and if you become suddenly confused, call us the same day or go to emergency. Book a review after the results. Anything else on your mind before you go?
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): right, I'll do that. Thank you, doctor

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Doctor, hi, where would you like me to put my coat?
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Of course, leave it there. How can I help?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm here because of red, cracked skin on my hands.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since when exactly?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm not sure when it began, to be honest. Some weeks ago, but I can't say how many.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood. Okay, give me more detail on it, whatever comes to mind.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Only moisturiser, and it's not much. Yes, gloves and washing hands. That makes it worse. About a three out of ten.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is there anything else with it?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): It usually comes with stinging when I wash up. With stinging when I wash up, a eight out of ten, I suppose. Yes, washing up. That makes it worse.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are you taking anything regularly, including from the pharmacy?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Hydrocortisone cream. I take it when needed. I'm supposed to take it regularly, but I don't always manage. Ah, I'm on moisturiser, several times a day.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long have you been on it?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): For two months.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about your medical history?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, I have eczema, for nearly five years.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, right. Yes, eczema is known to us, good to have that clear. Tell me about your routine, work, habits, that sort of thing.
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Lots of rice, lentils and some fruit. I do a yoga class on Thursdays. My partner and our baby.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are there any allergies I should be aware of?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm allergic to trimethoprim, I get itching.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any nail changes or fever at all?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Erm, no, none that I've noticed.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did you get new soap or cream or rash elsewhere?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): I haven't had new soap or cream or rash elsewhere, no.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with the waterworks?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): No, um, that's all fine.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pins and needles or loss of strength anywhere?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing odd there.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Time for your numbers, if that's okay.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep your arm relaxed for me...
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay: heart rate 85, blood pressure 124 over 72, temp 36.9 degrees, oxygen saturation is 98 percent.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that normal?
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, I'll interpret them after the examination.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Shall I start the examination?
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does that hurt?
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): The skin on both hands is red, dry and cracked in the finger creases, with no weeping.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's the examination finished.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): From what you've told me and what I found, it fits best with irritant hand dermatitis. Another possibility is allergic contact dermatitis. Stop me if I've got anything wrong. You've had red, cracked skin on your hands, and no rash elsewhere or new soap or cream.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, um, that's right.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): I think a patch test makes sense here, for dermatitis.
[SEG0040] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can book that for Tuesday at 2 pm.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Use gloves for washing up and moisturise straight after you dry your hands. Come back if it hasn't settled in two weeks.
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): I can manage that.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's everything on my side. Anything you're unsure about?
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor, goodbye.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, goodbye for now.

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Um, sorry, doctor, shall I sit here?
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, come in. Please sit. How can I help you?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Erm, um, so the thing is, I've got not opening my bowels.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did it come on recently?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Well, it's been nearly five years, I'm fairly sure. I thought it would sort itself out, but it hasn't.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me a bit more about it: how bad it gets, how often, and whether anything makes it better or worse.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Moderate, I'd say. It settles a little with prune juice. And, And there's a bloated tummy as well, four weeks now. Ah, I've also had hard small stools, for about three months.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you have any chronic illnesses?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): An underactive thyroid, for nearly five years. Sorry, I know I'm rambling a bit.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are you allergic to anything? Any allergies to medicines or foods?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry, uh, what was I saying, yes, amoxicillin, it gives me hives.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which medicines do you take at the moment?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Yeah, you know, I take Thyronorm, 50 micrograms, every morning for my thyroid.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you drink alcohol?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): I only drink at family occasions.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any smoking?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): I have about eight cigarettes in a day.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): How are your meals?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): I grab fast food at lunch most days.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, how active are you?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): I hardly move around during the day.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your job?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): I work in accounts at a hospital.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): What operations have you had, if any?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): I mean, just my appendix taken out, when I was in my twenties.

[SEG0051] person_1 (PATIENT): Right.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): I think we're done unless you have questions.
[SEG0053] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor, goodbye.

[SEG0043] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can book that that for Thursday at 9 am

[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): alright, I'll be back
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): right, that's the plan do you wanna ask me anything?
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): right, no, that's all. Thanks a lot
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): See you soon.

[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): I will, doctor, I will. Thanks very much now.

[SEG0001] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come in, Brendan, sit down. I have the note from your last visit here, and it seems Maureen is worried about your weight.
[SEG0002] person_1 (PATIENT): She is, doctor, and so am I now, to be honest. I can't stop thinking about it.
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Tell me in your own words what's been happening.
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm losing weight. My trousers are hanging off me, and the belt's on the last hole now.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since when, roughly?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): About three months. Maybe a bit longer. Is that very bad? Should I be worried?
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's find out first. Has your appetite changed?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm off my food, yeah. Maureen did a roast on Sunday and I couldn't finish it, which never happens.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything else you've noticed alongside that?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm tired too. Wrecked by the afternoon, even when I've done nothing at all.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting at all?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood in your stool, or black motions?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Not that I've seen. Is that something I should be looking for?
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's a standard question. What about a cough that won't shift?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No cough. My chest has been grand.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had fevers?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No fevers. I'd be at the thermometer all day, I'm that anxious.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): And any trouble swallowing your food?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): No, it all goes down fine. I just don't want it.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about passing water, any trouble there?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): No, that's all normal.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Let's go through your health history. What are you being treated for?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): High blood pressure and high cholesterol. And an underactive thyroid. And reflux, now and then.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what tablets are you on for those?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): Ramipril, 5 mg once a day, for the blood pressure. And atorvastatin, 20 mg at night, for the cholesterol.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the third one?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): The thyroid tablet. 75 micrograms, maybe? I'd have to look at the box to be sure.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair enough, we'll check that. Have you had any surgery over the years?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): I had my appendix out when I was twelve. And a knee replacement about six years ago.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Penicillin. I came out in a rash all over, years ago. My mother never let me forget it.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted. Is there anything serious in the family?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): My father had bowel cancer. And my mother had a stroke. That's why I'm so on edge about all this.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's understandable. Do you smoke, Brendan?
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): I stopped smoking fifteen years ago. Twenty a day for years before that, though.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): And alcohol?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): I drink a couple of pints on a Saturday, and that's the height of it.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you do for work, or are you retired?
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Retired, I was a postman for thirty years. I live with Maureen, just the two of us now.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, let me take your vitals, and then have a feel of your tummy.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure 138 over 84, pulse 88, temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius, oxygen 97 percent, and your weight is 71 kilograms.
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that good or bad?
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mostly fine. The weight is the one that tells the story. Now lie back for me.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your tummy is soft and there's no tenderness. There are no lumps in your neck either.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank God. So what is it, doctor?
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): I can't say for sure yet. My leading suspicion is that your thyroid tablet is a bit too strong for you, which can cause weight loss.
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): And the bowel cancer, with my father? I keep thinking about it.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): We're going to rule things out properly. I'll order blood tests today, including your thyroid.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): And I'd like a stool sample too, to be thorough, given your father's history. I'll give you a pot.
[SEG0051] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. Is there anything I should be doing in the meantime?
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Three things. Eat little and often, add full-fat milk and butter where you can, and weigh yourself once a week.
[SEG0053] person_1 (PATIENT): Weekly. Maureen will love that.
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): And don't change any tablets yourself. Bring the thyroid box in so we can check the dose.
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you lose any more weight before the results are back, ring me straight away and I'll see you sooner.
[SEG0056] person_1 (PATIENT): I will, doctor. Thank you, I feel a little calmer now.

[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hello, Mrs Brennan. Is that right, short of breath on the way to the bathroom?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Well, it's not that bad. I get a bit puffed.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mum, you have to sit down on the landing. Every time.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did it start?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh, a while ago. A month? Two? I don't keep track.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'd say it's been six weeks, since the cold, but I'm not certain either, Mum was already slow before it.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll note that neither of you is sure. Any chest pain?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): No pain. No.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any swelling of your legs, or a cough?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): My ankles puff up by evening. No cough.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): What tablets are you on?
[SEG0013] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Bisoprolol, 5 mg once a day, and furosemide, 40 mg in the morning.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what are those for?
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her heart, she has heart failure, and high blood pressure.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Who is at home with you, Mrs Brennan?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): I live alone. Sheila here pops in every day.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me listen to your chest. ~
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Go on.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): The heart sounds are regular, and there are fine crackles at the bottom of both lungs. ~
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is it her heart, doctor? ~
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): With the heart failure history, and the ankle swelling, I'd say this is likely her heart failure getting worse, with fluid building up.
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh, I see. ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's treatable. I'd like to arrange blood tests and a heart scan, an echocardiogram, to see how the heart is pumping.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Will she need to go into hospital? ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not today, if you can both watch her closely. The blood tests today, and the scan in the next two weeks.
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. ~
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please weigh her each morning, and ring me if her weight rises by two kilos in three days, or she's breathless at rest.
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will. ~
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to see you both in a week, to check how she is and look at the blood results.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A week. Thank you, doctor. ~

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): G'day. It's my feet. They burn. Mostly at night. Drives me mad.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has that been going on?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Eight months, nearly. It started in my toes, and now it's the whole of both feet.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Can you describe it?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Like they've been dipped in hot water, or a pins and needles. Sheets feel too heavy.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does it affect your hands, or other parts? ~
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): No, only the feet, so far. ~
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any weakness, or tripping over things? ~
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I can walk fine. ~
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you taking at the moment?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Metformin, 1000 mg twice a day, for my diabetes.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is the diabetes well controlled? ~
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): It was a bit high at my last check, 60-something. ~
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Gabapentin. I had a swollen face, a few years back. The GP said never again.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's important, thank you. Let me check your feet. Take your socks off. ~
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Right.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your skin is dry, and you've lost some feeling to light touch on the soles of both feet, and the vibration sense is reduced at the toes, but the pulses are good.
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that the diabetes? ~
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): This looks like diabetic nerve damage, peripheral neuropathy, I'd say.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it permanent? ~
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): The damage can't always be reversed, but better sugar control stops it getting worse, and the burning can be treated. ~
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): What do we do? ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to arrange a blood test for your sugar control, the HbA1c, and your vitamin B12, as metformin can lower it, and other causes need ruling out.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Fine. ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since you can't take gabapentin, I'd like to think about a different pain treatment once we have the results. ~
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. ~
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Meanwhile, check your feet every day for blisters or cuts, wear well-fitting shoes, and never walk barefoot.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): I walk barefoot all the time. ~
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not any more, I'm afraid. Your feet can't warn you if you tread on something. ~
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Right. ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you notice a sore that doesn't heal, a blister, or any redness or swelling, come in the same day.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): I will. Thanks. ~

[SEG0001] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, please, my husband, he ate prawns, and now his lips are swelling, and he's coming out in hives!
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bring him straight in, sit him up. Sir, can you tell me your name, and how you're feeling? ~
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Peter. My lips feel huge. And my throat's a bit tight.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did you eat the prawns?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Twenty minutes ago. A prawn curry, at the Thai place.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, it was ten minutes. We'd only just got to the car, I looked at my watch. ~
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): It doesn't matter exactly, we're acting now. Any trouble breathing?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Not really. I'm fine, I can breathe.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's wheezing, doctor, listen to him.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll listen. Have you had a reaction like this before? ~
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Never. I've eaten prawns all my life. ~
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines or other foods, as far as you know?

[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check you. Pulse, oxygen, pressure. ~

[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pulse 112, blood pressure 102 over 60, oxygen 95 percent, temperature 36.8, respiratory rate 22.
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is that bad? ~
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your pulse is fast, the oxygen is a little low, and the pressure is on the low side, which is concerning. Open your mouth, Peter. ~
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Ahh.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your lips and tongue are swollen, there are raised red hives over your chest and arms, and I can hear a wheeze in your chest.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it serious? ~
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, it's what we call anaphylaxis, a severe reaction to the prawns. We're treating it now.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh God. ~
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nurse, I want you to give adrenaline, intramuscular, point five of a milligram, into his thigh, now. And oxygen, and a drip.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Will I be all right? ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. The adrenaline works fast. You'll feel your heart race for a few minutes. ~
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Can I stay with him? ~
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, please, hold his hand. I'm also going to give an antihistamine and a steroid by injection, and we'll keep you in for at least six hours, to watch for a second reaction.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay. ~
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): And I'd like a blood test for tryptase, which shows the reaction, and a repeat set of observations every fifteen minutes.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thank you, doctor. ~
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Peter, don't eat or drink anything, and tell the nurse if your breathing worsens.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): I will. ~

[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Where is the tummy pain?

[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): No vomiting. A little nausea.

[SEG0015] person_3 (NURSE): Doctor, his observations. Temperature 39.2, pulse 84, blood pressure 108 over 66, oxygen 97 percent, respiratory rate 20.

[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): No allergies.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you take any tablets?

[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm a chef.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me examine your tummy.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Ahh, it hurts. ~
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your tummy is tender in the lower right, and there's a mild fullness, and I can feel your spleen tip.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it appendicitis? ~

[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Will my family be at risk? ~

[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll be careful. ~
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Faith will arrange the ward, and I'll see you there this evening.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. ~

[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): No, he's at work. He said he'd come to the next one. ~
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's fine. Can you tell me about your periods? Are they regular?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Mostly. Every twenty-eight to thirty days, I'd say.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain with the periods, or with intercourse?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Quite painful periods, yes. Intercourse is fine.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you ever been pregnant before?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): No, never. This is the first time we've tried.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any previous problems with your womb or ovaries, like cysts or fibroids?

[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or drink alcohol?

[SEG0017] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Blood pressure 118 over 74, pulse 70, weight 62 kilograms, height 165 centimetres.

[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your tummy is soft and not tender, and I don't feel any lumps.

[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take care now.

[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, come in and sit down. What brings you here today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Okay, so doctor, I'll sit in if that's okay, I know what's been happening.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, good, that'll be useful. Pull up a chair.
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Hmm, I've been dealing with an irregular heartbeat.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has this been bothering you? Bear with me, I'm just building up the picture.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): It's been three days, I'm fairly sure.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is it a lot or only a little?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Mostly mild.
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): I, I was just going to say that the main thing is—
[SEG0011] person_4 (NURSE): Sorry to cut in, doctor, quick question: shall I bring the trolley in now or later?
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Later, thanks. Please go on. Any occasional bruising as well?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, uh, actually. Being short of breath on slopes was there, you know, but it's gone away on its own.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, have you had an irregular heartbeat before, or is this the first time?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): A bit, about six months ago. It settled by itself back then.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has anything ever caused you a reaction? I mean any allergies.
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Erm, you know, I think I reacted to some antibiotic once, years ago. I don't remember which one, or what happened exactly.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you have any long-term conditions?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): Right, I have an irregular heartbeat, for about a year. I've been putting this off for weeks. Arthritis in my knees, for two years.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you ever had an operation?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay, so I had a varicose vein procedure last year.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you take any prescribed or over-the-counter medicines?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm, I'm on paracetamol, 650 milligrams, when needed.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She is supposed to take it when needed, but I can't say she always does.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you drink alcohol?
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing, I'm teetotal.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): How about smoking?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): I smoke roughly a pack every two days.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your job?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): I work in accounts at a hospital.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any black stools?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): No, no black stools.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you noticed fainting, nosebleeds or chest pain?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): No, not a single one.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about your tummy and bowels, anything unusual there?
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing unusual, no.
[SEG0038] person_4 (NURSE): Here are the numbers, doctor. Heart rate 116, oxygen saturation is 97 percent. Temp 37.1 degrees, pressure 120 over 85, respiratory rate 16.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, noted. Going by what you've described, the most likely explanation is atrial fibrillation, rate reasonably controlled. We shouldn't forget anaemia from bleeding.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): I think kidney function tests makes sense here, for anticoagulant dosing.
[SEG0041] person_5 (CLINICAL_STAFF): We have a slot Monday at 10 am, if that works.
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): That's fine.
[SEG0043] person_4 (NURSE): I've already done an ECG, it's ready for you.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, that helps. I'm going to order a full blood count, for anticoagulant review. Never skip the blood thinner, and tell any dentist or surgeon you take it. Keep an eye out, and if the symptoms get worse, call us the same day or go to emergency.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): Alright, I follow.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Book a review in three months. Can you run through the plan with me quickly, just to be certain?
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): So, I come back in three months. Is that right?
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, exactly right. Does all of that make sense?
[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor, goodbye.

[SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Hello? Doctor? I was told to come in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Of course, leave it there. How can I help?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Mainly sudden shortness of breath. There's a couple of other things, but that's the main one.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Understood. How frequently does it come?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Honestly, a few times a day.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you been coughing up a little blood?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): Ah, um, yes, for one week.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's start with the basic checks.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nearly done with the readings...
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay: blood pressure 139 over 89, pulse 98, saturation 90 percent, temperature is 36.7 degrees, respiratory rate 24.
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that okay?
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll interpret them after the examination.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Could you come over to the couch, please?
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Does that hurt?
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your left calf is swollen and tender, and your oxygen is lower than I'd like.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good, you can sit up again.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): A few quick ones: fever, chest tightness or wheeze?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): I haven't had fever, chest tightness or wheeze, no.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, anything with your nerves, like weakness or numbness?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Actually, no, that's all normal.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything unusual with passing urine?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Nothing there, uh, no.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Can you list what you take, tablets, creams or inhalers?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): Allopurinol. I take it 100 milligrams, once a day. I've never really been one for hospitals.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long have you taken that?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): About about a year. I take something called napr... naproxen, 250 milligrams, maybe, twice a day for the knee pain.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you got the box or the prescription on you?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): No, it's at home. It's alendronate, 70 milligrams, once a week for my bones.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, carry on. A few questions about your lifestyle now.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): I walk the dog every morning. I retired from the post office two years ago. I drink a lot of tea and snack through the day.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any previous surgeries?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Well, no, not at all.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any health conditions I should have on record? Just so I get the full picture.
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): I've, I've had gout, yes. I'd rather know what's going on than keep guessing.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): And besides that?
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): I have arthritis in my knees, for nearly five years. Thin bones, for five years.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm, okay. Yes, arthritis in your knees and thin bones are known to us, good to have that clear.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Before we go further, any allergies?
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): Years back I got a rash all over from amoxicillin, so I stay away from it now.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): From what you've told me and what I found, I think we're dealing with a possible blood clot in the lung at this stage.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm scared it's something bad. Is it?
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's reasonable to be concerned, but right now a possible blood clot in the lung is my leading thought, not anything worse. Let's get a CT scan of the chest, for breathlessness. The result will help us decide whether anything more is needed. You need to go to hospital now for a scan. And please bring the latest prescription or the medicine boxes to the next visit, so we can settle the dose.
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, that's clear.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to see you again straight away. Does all of that make sense?

[SEG0059] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take care now.

[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): How frequently does it come?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): It's, It's a couple of times a week.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you noticed anything else alongside it?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): An itchy rash first goes along with it, most of the time. Oh, you know, the itchy rash first? That's been for six months.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll do your observations first.

[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nearly finished here.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): There are firm, tense blisters on a red base on the arms and legs.
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Right.

[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, no, none of those at all.

[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): So, um, I had part of my thyroid removed years back.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything in your past medical history I should know?
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): High blood pressure, for nearly five years.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about alcohol?
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): I'll have a glass of wine with dinner.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): I've never touched a cigarette.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): How active are you?
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): I hardly move around during the day.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is there someone at home?
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): My husband and I live above the shop.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you do during the day?
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): I look after my grandchildren most days.

[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Look after yourself.

[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which medicines do you take at the moment?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Let me think, I'm on paracetamol, when needed.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): How much do you take?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): It's, It's 1 gram.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many days or weeks has it been?

[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any joint swelling, fever or rash?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No joint swelling, fever or rash, none of it.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): How about your heart, any problems like that?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing with my heart.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Who lives with you?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): My partner and our baby.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, anything you do to stay fit?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): I do a yoga class on Thursdays.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to tablets, food or anything in the environment?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing as far as I know.

[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): No, no conditions.

[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your joints are not swollen and you are tender over many muscle points.

Do get help quickly if the symptoms get worse. Let's review you in six weeks.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything else on your mind before you go?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, that's helpful.

[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): You are hot, shaking and your blood pressure is low, and you had chemotherapy nine days ago.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not really. It's normal.

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, well. By evening there's a mild ache in the groin. I sit down and it settles. It's nothing, really.

[SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, come through. Sorry, the corridor fan is rattling like anything today.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, I can't hear myself think with that noise. It's ok, I won't sit long, this is nothing much.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Let me take the readings first. Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Pulse seventy-six. Temperature thirty-six point seven.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Oxygen is ninety-eight percent. Breathing sixteen a minute. Weight is sixty-two kilos today.

[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Wait, err, I read the pulse wrong. It is seventy-eight, not seventy-six.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Have a seat. What brought you today?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, it's the sneezing and the running nose, every spring only. I have overdone it in the garden again, that's all.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Every spring. This spell, how long has it been?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Two three weeks. I can't tell you the exact day, sometime early April maybe. Mild only, my wife forced me to come.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Even if it feels small, how does a day actually go?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): These two three weeks it's sneezing in bouts, worse if I have been in the garden, nose running like a tap that won't shut. Every spring the same story. Mornings I get a frog in my throat. Eyes itch a bit, all mild only.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): The eyes. Are they watering as well as itching?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it spoil your sleep at night?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes not really.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze, any whistling sound in the chest?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No wheeze. Chest is perfectly fine.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): And cough, shortness of breath, or fever with this?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough, no breathing problem, no fever. I am telling you it's a small thing.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any tablets you are already on for it?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Cetrizine, ten mg. They told me once a day by mouth. I take it sometimes only, when the sneezing is too much, not daily.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): So daily was the advice and sometimes is what happens. Any other medicine, and any allergies to tablets or anything else?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No other tablets. No allergies. My sister is allergic to dust, that is her problem, not mine.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Noted. What work do you do, any smoking, who is at home?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Accounts job, sitting only. I never smoked. A flat with my wife and two kids, and a bit of Sunday gardening.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any asthma or eczema before, or any surgery?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No asthma, no eczema. No operation ever. Healthy only, what to do.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nasal lining is pale and a little boggy. Eyes are mildly red. Chest is clear, no wheeze when I listen.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): See, nothing. Some afternoons I feel like a wet rag, but that is just the heat, not this nose thing.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): You're putting that down to the heat. Are your feet numb at all, or was the chair just uncomfortable?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): My feet feel dead in that waiting chair only. I walk two steps and it's gone. Forget it.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't chase the feet or the heat. About two to three weeks of sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes and morning throat irritation, the same every spring. No wheeze, no cough and no fever, and the cetirizine ten mg was meant once a day but taken only sometimes. No allergies yourself, your sister has the dust allergy, and you don't smoke, is that fair?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, that's correct. Don't make it a big case, doctor.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am not going to call this asthma, the chest doesn't support that. My working impression is seasonal allergic rhinitis, though it could also be simple irritant rhinitis from the garden dust and pollen. I can't separate those two fully today. I'm not waiting to see what the tests say, so no bloods and no scans.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll stop the cetrizine ten mg tablet by mouth from today. For the sneezing and the runny nose I'm changing you to fexofenadine, one hundred and eighty mg, one tablet by mouth once a day, right through this season.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): And for the itchy eyes, olopatadin drops, zero point one percent, one drop in each eye twice a day.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Fexo is fine. Drops also if you insist. Uh, I will forget the night one, I know myself.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Put a phone reminder morning and night so the drops actually get used. Don't take cetirizine on top of the new tablet. Windows shut on heavy pollen days, a saline rinse if the nose is pouring, and a mask when you garden.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok ok. So I come only if it gets worse, or what?
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in four weeks, that visit is booked with me, even if you still think it is nothing. If you start wheezing or the eyes swell, come sooner and don't wait the four weeks.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Four weeks, fine. I'll tell my wife you people worry too much.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): I'll hold the four-week slot at the desk. Collect the prescription on the way out.

[SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in. What can I do for you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the sneezing, doctor, and the itchy eyes and the runny nose. It comes every spring and I'm going through tissues like nobody's business, and the garden out the back is in full bloom which doesn't help one bit.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh it's been five years... no, six years, I was counting from the wrong summer. We moved in twenty nineteen and this is the sixth spring in the house, so six.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Only in the spring?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the spring, yes, from about March until June. The rest of the year I'm grand, not a sniffle, uh, which is why I left it so long, I kept thinking it would pass on its own.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Worse at any particular time?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): When I'm cutting the grass, or if I'm out in the garden in the evening, it goes mad altogether. Inside with the windows shut it's a small bit better, though the sneezing still comes in fits.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No wheeze, no. I can walk the dog up the hill without getting tight, I was half afraid it was asthma but there's no whistle in the chest at all.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough either. It's all in the nose and the eyes, um, the throat gets a bit scratchy from the dripping but I'm not coughing.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both eyes?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Both eyes, they itch something fierce and they water, especially the left one in the mornings. I look like I've been crying at the school gate and it's mortifying, truly.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): On any treatment?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Ceterizine from the chemist, I take it sometimes, not every day. I thought the dose was twenty milligrams but no, it's ten milligrams, I was mixing it up with a painkiller I had years ago. When I do take it the sneezing eases a small bit but the eyes stay itchy.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing else, I don't even take a vitamin. My sister is forever at me to take one but I don't, I forget them.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Drug allergies?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I know of. My sister is allergic to dust though, she gets wheezy and her eyes swell, she's on a spray from her own GP, but I've never had a reaction to a medicine myself.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone else in the family?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, just her. My parents are grand, no asthma, no hay fever, and my brother is the same, it's only herself with the dust.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Blood pressure is one thirty-two over eighty-four... no, one twenty-eight over seventy-six. Pulse seventy-two. Oxygen ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Eyes are red, conjunctiva injected both sides. Nasal mucosa pale and boggy. Chest clear, no wheeze.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Is the redness bad? I've been rubbing them, I know I shouldn't, and I tried cold teabags last week which did nothing, and the chemist said not to use some old steroid drops I found in the press.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any stomach symptoms?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, stomach's perfect, I eat fine, no heartburn, no change in the bowel. I was going to mention the heartburn I had in pregnancy years ago but that's long gone, not relevant now I suppose.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): This is seasonal allergic rhinitis. Hay fever.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I thought as much. My sister said the same at Easter, going on about dust mites and hoovering, err, but mine is only the spring so it has to be the pollen, the birch at the end of the road especially.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stop the cetirizine. Skin prick test with the nurse Thursday morning. No antihistamine from now until after that test.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday morning, grand, I don't start until half ten so I'm free. Will I need to fast, or is it just the arm?
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): No fasting. Just the forearm. If the skin prick is borderline we'll do a specific IgE blood test.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): And if it's not borderline, do we still do the bloods or leave them?
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leave them. After the test start loratadine ten milligrams once a day... no, fexofenadine, a hundred and eighty milligrams once a day.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Once a day, by mouth, even on days I feel grand? I was only taking the ceterizine sometimes so a daily tablet is a change for me.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Every day through the season. Olopatadine drops, one drop each eye twice a day, start those today.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice a day, both eyes, even the left that's worse? I'll keep them in the fridge if that's allowed, or does the chemist say room temperature, I always get mixed up with drops.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Room temperature is fine. I'll see you in two weeks with the result.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it has not settled in six weeks, we'll arrange a sinus scan.

[SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, in you come. Blood pressure's one twenty eight over seventy... no, sorry, one eighteen over seventy four, and your pulse is seventy two beats a minute. Pop yourself down.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. Is one eighteen bad? I've been in a right state about it all morning.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): No, love, that's a normal blood pressure. My sister's was sky high last year and they started her on tablets, totally different kettle of fish.
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She was up half the night googling. I told her it could wait till we actually got here.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr Okonkwo. What can I do for you today?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, it's the sneezing. Every spring it kicks off and I just can't cope with it.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay. Talk me through what actually happens.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Well my nose runs, my eyes itch like mad, and I sneeze all day. It happens every spring when the pollen's about.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's been through a box of tissues a day since the trees came out. Keeps rubbing at her eyes.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long has this spring's bout been going on?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, about three weeks... no, actually it's been five weeks. I lost count.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Is this going to turn into asthma? My neighbour ended up in hospital and I've been panicking.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll get to that. Any wheeze, or a tight chest?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No wheeze. I keep listening and there's nothing.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Cough? Shortness of breath?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough, and I'm not breathless. Honestly.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. Are you taking anything for it at the moment?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Citirizine. I take it sometimes, not every day. The packet says ten milligrams... no, hang on, mine are the five milligram ones. I checked this morning.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Cetirizine, yes. The usual advice is once a day. So you're not doing that?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only when the sneezing's really bad. Maybe three days a week? I'm not sure I stick to it properly.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): Anything else, prescribed or over the counter?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I tried a nasal spray years back, Beconase, but I stopped it.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): What made you stop?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): It stung my nose and I didn't think it was doing anything. That was ages ago.
[SEG0025] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry, quick one. Peak flow outside was four hundred and twenty litres a minute. My own asthma's been grumbling with this pollen, I've had to up my inhaler.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Four twenty is a perfectly decent peak flow. Any allergies yourself, to medicines or anything else?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that I know of. My sister's allergic to dust, really badly, but I'm not. They tested me years ago.
[SEG0028] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Her sister, not mine. I nearly chipped in that my little boy gets eczema, but that's nothing to do with her.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): The test, what did they actually tell you?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): It was a blood test at the hospital. They said it was borderline for pollen. I never got the number, and I can't remember which year.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright. We won't treat a borderline result we can't see as gospel. Let me look at your nose and eyes.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): The lining of your nose is pale and boggy. Your eyes are watery, but the whites aren't badly red.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): What's happening is pollen sticks to the lining and your body releases histamine. That histamine makes the lining swell and itch, and it sets off the sneezing. It isn't damaging the tissue.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Histamine? Is that dangerous long term? Am I damaging my nose every year? Sorry, I ask too much.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): You're not damaging it. Same chemical on the surface of the eyes, which is why they itch and water. Nothing I'm seeing suggests harm.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): So I won't go blind or anything. I know that sounds daft.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): You won't. Any fever, or do you feel unwell in yourself?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I feel fine in myself, just fed up with the sneezing.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): And your tummy, your waterworks, any trouble there?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. All normal.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. I think this is hay fever, seasonal allergic rhinitis. Cetirizine a few days a week isn't really holding it. I'd switch you to fexofenadine, one hundred and eighty milligrams, one tablet once a day by mouth, and add sodium cromoglicate eye drops.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Fexo-what? Will that make me drowsy? I drive to the office every day.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fexofenadine. It's a non-drowsy antihistamine. Stop the cetirizine when you start it, don't take both. The drops are one drop in each eye four times a day.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Four times a day, I'll forget, what if I miss one? And one hundred and eighty, isn't that huge? I read ten was the dose, wait, that was the citirizine, not this new one.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, ten was the figure on the old packet, and yours are five milligrams. One hundred and eighty is the normal adult dose of fexofenadine, not too much. If you miss a drop, just do the next one.
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I can remind her about the drops. I already do my dad's, he's got glaucoma, so I'm used to eye drops.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Are the drops safe with contact lenses? I wear them for work. And can this get worse every year? I was reading at two in the morning.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take the lenses out, put the drop in, and leave them out for fifteen minutes. Screens and lenses can dry the eyes a bit but they don't cause this pattern. Try not to rub.
[SEG0049] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She does work in an office, lots of screens. I keep saying take breaks.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'd like you back in four weeks so we can see if this has settled. Reception will book it.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Four weeks, okay. What if I get wheezy before then? Do I just wait?
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): No. If you start wheezing or you get breathless, come back sooner, don't wait the four weeks. Start both medicines today if the chemist has them.

[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He didn't want to come. I had to drag him from the godown gate.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one thirty eight over eighty four. Pulse seventy six. Saturation 98 percent.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm doctor Shah. Sit comfortably. What has been bothering you?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Bothering is a big word. Umm, there is a small lump, right side groin. Comes when I lift, goes when I lie down. That's all.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mm. Tell me a bit more, in your own words. When did you first notice it?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, three four months back I think. I didn't mark any date. It is not troubling me much.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He says that, but in the evening he is pressing it and making a face. My sister, she had a groin swelling last year, got operated in her town, so I got scared for him.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): I understand why you worried. Does the lump pain, or is it only the swelling?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Little bit ache only, by evening, after the shift. Morning the lump itself I forget.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): And vomiting? Any of that?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No vomiting. I am eating my rice as usual.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fever? Or the skin over it turning red?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Skin is normal, not red. See, nothing.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Also, uh, when I push it with my hand it goes in. Simple.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good that it goes back. Let me examine you. Please stand up and cough.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. There is a soft swelling in the right groin, it bulges when you cough, and it reduces when I press. Left groin is clear. Abdomen is soft, no tenderness.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Told you. Small only.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): What I feel is most likely a right inguinal hernia. A little bit of bowel is slipping through a weak spot in the groin muscle. Strain pushes it out, lying down lets it fall back.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): So the intestine is coming out? Sounds dramatic. People in the godown have this and they still load.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): It can stay quiet for a long time, true. The worry is if the bowel gets stuck and the blood supply is cut. That is an emergency, not a small thing.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Then what do we do, doctor? He will not sit at home.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): We will come to the lifting. Before that, any illnesses you already have, any tablets?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Pressure, only mild. I take amlodipin, five milligram, one in the morning. Nothing else.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright, blood pressure is ongoing, amlodipine five mg every morning. Family side, anyone with sugar, heart problems, pressure?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not have sugar or any such thing, my elder brother had a heart attack around sixty, and another sister has pressure but no sugar.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): And day to day, the work, food, exercise, any alcohol?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I am a loader at the godown near the highway, twelve hour shifts, six days a week. Food is rice and dal, whatever the canteen puts, and I don't do exercise separately, the loading is the exercise. Whisky, one peg, two times in a week, not more than that.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): That is heavy work for this. Please don't lift the full sacks for now. If something light has to be moved, bend the knees, hold it close, and don't strain while holding the breath.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, if I tell the supervisor no lifting, he will put someone else on my spot. The lump is tiny.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): I hear the job worry, truly. A stuck hernia will take you off work for longer than lighter duty will. I am sending you to the general surgeon, we will book that from this clinic.
[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): I will enter the surgical referral before you go. My own child had a small procedure last month, the surgery waiting room fills by nine, so reach a little early when they give the date.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Early, late, all this running around. Fine, we will go.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the lump will not go back in, or the pain becomes severe, or you start vomiting, come to emergency the same day.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya ya. If it sticks I will come. Otherwise no drama.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): And come back to see me in six weeks, once the surgeon has seen you, so we know how the lifting is going.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will make sure he comes. Left to him he will say next month next month.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): The amlodipine, are you actually taking it every morning?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Most mornings. Umm, the shift is from five sometimes, I forget. Maybe two times in a week I miss.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Try not to miss it, especially if an operation comes up. Keep the strip near the bed so the early shift doesn't steal it.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Hmm. Okay, I will keep it there.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): I have noted one thirty eight over eighty four and pulse seventy six on the paper for the surgeon.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Those are fine for today. Any other question in your mind?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): You are not giving any tablet for the lump, no?
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): No new tablet for the lump from my side. The surgeon will talk about repair. The ache you can watch, it is mild.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. Less tablets the better. The bus was packed today, anyway.
[SEG0048] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Thank you doctor. We will do the early morning thing and the no heavy sack thing.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take care, both of you. Go slow with the sacks till the surgeon says otherwise.

[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Arm strength is normal both sides. Speech is clear, I'm not hearing any slurring.

[SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, doctor. I've brought my brother, Mr Dlamini, through from the waiting room. Sorry if I seem half asleep, my little one was coughing the whole night.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Morning. Uh, have a seat, sir. What can I do for you today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. Thank you for fitting me in. I have come about a lump in the groin, the right side. It appears when I lift at work.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): A lump with lifting. How long have you noticed it?
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Three months, doctor. After a heavy shift he stands there holding the right side. I've seen it.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Forgive me, sister, that is not accurate. It has been six weeks, not three months. I do not wish to give you the wrong history, doctor.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mhm. You say six weeks, she says three months, so I'll put it down as roughly six weeks to three months. We won't settle it finer today. Tell me how the lump behaves.
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): If I lift a bag of cement, or push the wheelbarrow, the lump comes out. When I lie down on the bed it goes away completely. By the evening there is a mild ache, nothing severe.
[SEG0009] person_1 (NURSE): And he is up at night with it. I hear him in the passage, he can't sleep.
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): With respect, that is not the case. I sleep perfectly well. The ache is only in the evening, and it is mild. It does not wake me.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so it comes out with strain and slips back when you lie flat. Err, what I think is going on is a bit of bowel, or some fatty tissue, pushing through a weak spot in the groin muscle. The pressure of lifting forces it out, and lying down lets it drop back. That picture is an inguinal hernia, though I can't completely rule out a lymph node.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have not vomited.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nausea? Any change in the bowels? Pain in the tummy itself, apart from the groin?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No nausea, doctor. The bowels are regular, as usual. There is no pain in the tummy, only the groin.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And passing urine, any burning, or trouble getting it going?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No, doctor. That side of things is quite normal.
[SEG0018] person_1 (NURSE): Vitals while I remember. Blood pressure one nineteen over seventy-seven, ag no, wrong line, it's one oh nine over seventy-seven, pulse seventy-six, temperature thirty-six point four. Last time in March the pressure was one-forty over eighty-eight.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Those are comfortable numbers. Any allergy to medicines, Mr Dlamini?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): None, doctor. I have never reacted to a medicine.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): And what medicines are you actually taking?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Only Panado, two tablets at night, which is one gram, for the ache. I have used it for about two weeks. I did take broofen, four hundred milligrams, for the same ache, but I stopped that three weeks ago because it upset my stomach.
[SEG0023] person_1 (NURSE): There were Grandpa powders in his bag as well. I saw the box this morning.
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): That box belongs to a colleague on the site, doctor. I have never taken Grandpa powders myself.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then we ignore the Grandpa. Any operations in the past? Diabetes, heart problems, anything ongoing?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): No operations at all. No diabetes and no heart trouble, I am otherwise well. About two years ago the day hospital did a scan of the groin and they said the result was borderline. They did not call it a hernia at that time.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Borderline scan, and we haven't got the report in front of us, so I'll just note what you were told. Do you smoke?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): I have never smoked, doctor. I do take a beer on a Saturday after work, only the one.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the work itself is heavy, from what you've said.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. I am a manual labourer on a building site in Germiston. Cement, scaffolding, wheelbarrows. I stay in the back room at my sister's house.
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): Ja, he's with me. I leave for my clinic shift before he does, so I don't always see how he is in the morning. My own back has been sore from the extra shifts, but that's me, not him.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me examine you. Lie flat and cough for me. There is a soft swelling in the right groin, it bulges when you cough, and it reduces when I press it back. Nothing on the left, and the abdomen is soft and not tender.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): It is slightly sore when you press on the lump, doctor, if I may mention it. Not severely.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, I agree, mildly tender right over the swelling, and nowhere else. Well, I'm happy to call this a reducible right inguinal hernia. The lymph node is much less likely, now that it reduces so easily.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I don't think another scan will change the plan today. I'll refer you to the surgeons at the provincial hospital, and they'll send a clinic date. Until then, no heavy lifting. No cement bags, no wheelbarrows, no scaffolding.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the lump gets stuck out and you cannot push it back, or if you start vomiting, or the pain turns severe, go straight to casualty. Don't wait for the clinic.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): I understand, doctor. I will ask the foreman for lighter duties. Is an operation certain?
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): The surgeons will almost certainly discuss a repair, but that decision is theirs, not mine this morning. No new tablets from me. Carry on with the Panado at night if the ache is there, one gram, and don't go above that.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): May I still walk to work, doctor? It is about twenty minutes. I do not want to do harm.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Walking is fine. It is straining and heavy lifting I want stopped. If the ache builds on the walk, slow down, but ordinary walking should be alright. I won't book you back here routinely, the surgical clinic takes it from here.
[SEG0041] person_1 (NURSE): I'll take the referral letter to reception on the way out, they'll book the surgical clinic. And doctor, just so the file is straight, the March reading stays the old one. Today's pressure is the one oh nine over seventy-seven.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I am grateful for your time, and for the clear advice. I will be careful with the lifting.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Look after yourself, Mr Dlamini. Sister will sort the letter.
[SEG0044] person_1 (NURSE): Come, we'll get it stamped. You'll be alright.

[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Oh god, you're right, Galfer, three oh five, once a day. And Omprazole twenty milligrams at night for the heartburn.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Grand, so the legs are somewhere between a fortnight and three weeks, we'll not fight over the day. Were you on anything for the blood pressure before the pregnancy?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Mizartan, for the pressure. Twenty milligrams I think. I stopped it the week I found out, the hospital said stop. Is the baby all right with all these tablets, I keep panicking.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): The folic acid and the iron are there for the baby, and Omprazole is used a lot in pregnancy. I wouldn't be worried on that score. Any headache, flashing lights, or pain up under the ribs?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Could the creeping be a clot? My mam had a clot when she was having me. And my feet feel dead, like, I don't even know when that started.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll come to the clot in a minute, I want the headache answer first.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Oh. No. No headache, no lights, no pain under the ribs.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Any swelling of the legs, or chest pain?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No swelling. No chest pain. I walked up from the school yesterday and I've overdone it, I was puffing, but the chest wasn't sore.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're teaching still?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Senior infants, yeah. The room is so loud I can't hear myself think, but that's not why I'm in. I've a frog in my throat the last few days as well, is that the acid?
[SEG0020] person_4 (CAREGIVER): And she doesn't smoke, never has. I take Metformine myself for the sugar, that's nothing to do with her.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, Nuala, we'll leave your tablets out of it. How are the waterworks?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Grand. No bother there. Do I need one of those iron drips? I read about them at three in the morning.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not from what I'm hearing today. Let me have a look at the legs first.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): No swelling I can see. The pulses in both feet are there. The feet are a bit cool, that fits with what you're saying. I'm not thinking a clot.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): They told me the ferritin was eleven at the booking bloods. Is that why the legs are creeping? Will it harm the baby if I don't sleep?

[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): So what do I actually do tonight? If I stretch, if I have a bath, is that enough? And is the Omprazole definitely safe, you're sure?
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stretch the calves before bed, and a warm bath if you can get in and out grand. Stay on the folic acid and the Galfer, don't double the iron up yourself. Omprazole at the same dose is fine to keep going.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll send you for a ferritin and a full blood count this week. I'll see you back here in ten days with the results.
[SEG0030] person_1 (NURSE): And your midwife check is booked for Tuesday week at half nine. I'll leave the blood form at reception.
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): If the ferritin comes back grand and the legs are still at me, what then? Am I being stupid worrying?
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're not stupid. If they're still desperate when I see you, we can talk about other options then. If you get a bad headache, swelling of the face or hands, or the baby goes quiet, ring the hospital the same day.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): I am wrecked though. Err. Sorry for all the questions.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ask away, that's what we're here for. Mind yourself between this and the midwife.

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Neck's good. It's the elbow and that's it.

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stay with ibuprofen 400 milligrams with food, no more than three times a day. The Omprazole should cover your stomach. Come back in four weeks. Sooner if the fingers go numb or you can't hold a brush.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Four weeks. Yeah okay. It's really not that bad.

[SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this computer's crawling again. What's brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing, really. I nearly didn't come. Just a niggle in the left side, the loin, went down to the groin.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hang on, wrong window. Uh, say that again?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Left loin, shooting to the groin. Woke me about two this morning. It's eased. I wouldn't call it severe.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nought to ten, worst and right now?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm a four. Well actually a seven, maybe an eight, just for a few minutes. Now it's a two. Hardly there.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Were you sick?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, threw up the once in the night. Nothing since. Doesn't count.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood in the urine?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Wee was a bit pink this morning. Not blood, a tinge. Probably the light.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll read the dipstick. Blood three plus, protein trace, leucocytes negative, nitrites negative, glucose negative.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Three plus. They love a drama.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Obs from just now, temp 36.7, pulse 88, blood pressure 152 over 94, sats 97 percent. Left loin is tender, tummy soft, no guarding.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Only sore when you press. Rest of it is normal, like I said.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever or shivers, or stinging when you pass water?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Neither.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain on the right side at all?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest, breathing, all alright?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, fine.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medicines? Sorry, say it clearly, I clicked the cricket by mistake. No, I'm listening.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Just amlodopine, 5 milligrams every morning, for the blood pressure. Years. Nothing else.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None at all.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, while this request screen loads, have you seen the test? England are 240 for 4, Root's timing is lovely.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Had it on the radio till the traffic got me. The A38 was a car park, a good hour. Bloke said it's glorious out, proper shirt-sleeve weather. My neighbour's grandson has a club match Saturday if it holds, and I was more fed up about missing the morning session than anything.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ha. I might get the mower out if clinic ever ends. Lovely day for it. Sorry, screen's back.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): You're alright. I'm wasting your time anyway.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): I don't think you are. You've got the high blood pressure, I know. My impression is renal colic, likely a stone, but that's provisional, the scan has to confirm it. I'll start naproxen, 500 milligrams twice a day by mouth, with food, for five days, from today.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): If you insist. Seems a lot for a niggle.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse takes your bloods at eleven this morning, full blood count and kidney function. No need to fast, just drink some water beforehand. And a non-contrast CT of the kidneys is booked for two this afternoon.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Both today? Blimey.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): If those bloods are borderline we'll add a serum calcium, not otherwise. I'll see you back here in two weeks.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks is fine. I'll be right as rain.
